section_summary: This section contains Japanese legal instruments governing the post-World War II reorganization of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, including a Cabinet Order establishing the Local Liaison Committee and the full text of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Establishment Law (Law No. 120 of 1949) detailing the ministry's structure, bureaus, auxiliary organs, and regional Liaison and Coordination Offices. It also includes an August 1949 State Department memorandum by Niles W. Bond arranging the visit and policy briefing of Japanese diplomat Takeso Shimoda during his transit through the United States en route from the Paris ITU conference. The section concludes with a fragment of an earlier document bearing handwritten comments by Secretary of State George C. Marshall and a 1952 routing note from Taylor of NA requesting that it be indexed separately.

subfiles.summary: This legislation establishes the organization, mission, and statutory powers of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the National Government Organization Law. It defines the internal subdivisions—including the Minister's Secretariat and Bureaus of Political Affairs, Treaties, Research, Controls, and Liaison—as well as auxiliary organs such as the Foreign Service Training Institute and Central Liaison Committee. It also details the functions, jurisdictions, and locations of eleven regional Liaison and Coordination Offices and sets personnel provisions effective June 1, 1949.
subfiles.title: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs Establishment Law
